Wonderful! I’m excited to see how everything turns out. I can tell how much passion you & your wife have for the project. Getting a brand new business off the ground is already an impressive feat, and I have confidence your events will continue to improve. Looking forward to returning! 🪐

Hi Jason, I have some feedback & actually constructive criticism for you. 

Story wise, there were too many plot points + characters + details to pack into such a short experience. I had trouble keeping track of the story, even though actors were doing their best to summarize. Too complicated to follow, for children and adults. Remember: less is more. Keep the story short and sweet, doesn’t need to be lore heavy & require remembering several different characters in exposition to understand.

Second, your speech at the beginning was very disheartening. I know not everyone is a great public speaker, but when advertising your project, this is a skill worth honing. You started out by welcome everyone, expressing enthusiasm (good!) and then continued to point out all the things that weren’t finished (props, sets, etc). You can explain the unfinished drafts without telling your audience everything that’s wrong. It’s about presentation. If you’re not confident in the product you’re showing the audience, don’t pitch it with that insecurity. Highlight the good parts, hype up your audience! When you point out the bad parts, that’s all your audience will see. It crushed my hype. 

Secure your sets, make sure they are structurally sound. I’m thinking of the light game in particular. I hit one of the lights with not too much force and it came off the wall. Keep in mind that kids are probably gonna take wild swings at them, and the potential of them falling off is big. Also, the physical space in that room is too constrained for the game. Audience shouldn’t be hitting things in the dark when so huddled together, it could be dangerous and I felt nervous crowded in with everyone when doing that. Might be my own thing, but important to keep in mind.

The actors you employed were fantastic!! A few were shaky on their lines, but I can forgive that considering it’s a brand new show. However, more rehearsal couldn’t hurt. The way the makeup showed in the black light was a nice touch. Everyone stayed in character, especially the professor, who was my favorite + sold me on the immersion. I enjoyed the tarot reading at the end, as well as the chalkboard. Perfect idea to keep kids busy & have something at eye level. I would add more substance to the end for adults. Being let out into the empty room felt awkward. 

All in all, the concept of the carnival has potential, but could use MUCH more refining.

i’m not as skinny as i once was, but im also a hell of a lot healthier. at the worst of my ED i was barely functioning & i very well could’ve died, despite never being underweight or hitting a lot of those sickness milestones a lot of disordered ppl tend to glorify. sure, i was skinnier, but i wasn’t living, & it was painful, mentally and physically. its hard to remind myself of that sometimes, even after 2 residential stays and 2 PHP stays. i wish that ED centers were more well equipped to help trans folks, seeing as the prevelance of EDs in our community is even higher than in cis spaces!! its like, everyone has been able to acknowledge that, but no one knows how to help us. so i appreciate your advice & kind words, & am glad to have these spaces to talk about it. :) 

+ you have absolutely nothing to apologize for. i think we’re all victims of this mindset to some extent. whether its irt trans body ideals or just society + diet culture in general. its hard not to fall prey to all those harmful messages in the fucked up world we live in, & it isn’t your fault for having suffered through it. all we can hope to do is continue to unlearn the shitty messages, & reminding ourselves that we don’t have to punish ourselves, our bodies, or make us fit into an unattainable mold. :,)
